source: (text, request, material) => { const bad = []; const re = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { const s = (+m[1])*60+(+m[2]); const e = (+m[3])*60+(+m[4]); if (e <= s) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'span end not after start'}); } const d = text.match(/"duration"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/); if (d) { const dur = (+d[1])*60+(+d[2]); const re2 = /"span"\s*:\s*"(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s*[–-]\s*(\d{2}):(\d{2})"/g; while ((m = re2.exec(text))) { if ((+m[3])*60+(+m[4]) > dur) bad.push({start:m.index,end:m.index+m[0].length,why:'span runs past duration'}); } } return { ok: bad.length === 0, detail: bad.length ? bad.length + ' span problem(s)' : 'spans are mm:ss, ordered and inside duration', spans: bad }; }
means: Checks each span is mm:ss start–end, the end after the start and inside the clip duration.
